title: Cæsar Frederiks agtien-jarige reys, na en door Indien, anno 1563 en vervolgens, seer naauwkeurig door hem selfs beschreven. ; Nu aldereerst uyt het Engelsch vertaald. Met nodige konstprinten, en een volkomen register verrĳkt
shelf_note: A 1706 Dutch translation of Federici's account of travel in India. No tradition or collection is assigned, so there is nothing to conflict with. The page is plainly this work: the running head reads 'DOOR CÆSAR FREDERIKS.'
structure_note: The structure counts disagree with themselves: pages_translated is 0 but pages_translated_field is 80. Either the count or the field is stale. There are 4 printed backsteps and 5 repeats across 63 printed numbers. In an illustrated book ('Met nodige konstprinten') these are more likely misread numerals or unnumbered plates than a scan splice, but one page cannot settle it. On this leaf, page-num 19 and signature B 2 match the image.

pages.layout: single column of Dutch blackletter with roman for names; two marginal notes in the outer margin; running head with page number

ocr_errors.ocr: zijn 'er drie of vier gewapende Kusten
ocr_errors.problem: 'Fusten' (fustas, light galleys) misread as 'Kusten' (coasts), which makes no sense here. The translation silently corrects it to 'fustas'.

ocr_errors.ocr: Ik kwam in mijn reyse by getal ter plaats
ocr_errors.image: Jk quam in mijn reys by geval ter plaats
ocr_errors.problem: 'by geval' (by chance) misread as 'by getal' (by number). 'quam' is normalised to 'kwam' and 'reys' to 'reyse'. The translation follows the image ('by chance').

other.note: The running head 'BY CÆSAR FREDERIKS.' is translated as the first line of the reader text
The translation reads 'fustas' and 'by chance' where the served OCR has 'Kusten' and 'by getal'. The two panes disagree, although the English matches the image.

missing.english: from Cape Comori to the low land of Chilao
missing.why: 'Cape Comori' is Cape Comorin, the southern tip of India, and Chilao is Chilaw on the west coast of Ceylon. A general reader cannot place the pearl-fishery sea without this.

missing.english: being like the boats of our pilots
missing.why: 'Our' refers to the author's home waters (Venetian, carried over via the English). The comparison means little without a short note on what pilot boats were.

book_verdict: A clean page. The OCR has two moderate misreadings ('Kusten' for 'Fusten', 'getal' for 'geval') and some spelling normalisation; the translation is faithful to the image, and both glosses are correct. Nothing an expert would flag on sight, apart from the inconsistent translated-page counts in the record.
